For Petitioner(s) :Dr. Sunil Kumar Agarwal, AOR
                   Mr. Manoj Kumar Khanna, Adv.
                   Mr. Rishikesh Sharma, Adv.
                   Mr. Amarjeet Sahani, Adv.
                   Mr. Prakhar Dixit, Adv.
                   Mr. Aryan Kumar, Adv.
                   Ms. Anisha, Adv.
                   Ms. Shweta Bhardwaj, Adv.
                   Mrs. Mamta Singh, Adv.
                   Mr. Parvinder, Adv.
                   Mr. Virendra Kumar Pandey, Adv.
                   Mr. Firoz Siddique, Adv.
                   
                   
For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Delay condoned.
2. We have heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned
counsel for the respondent- Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir.
1

## Page 989

3. Petitioner has been convicted by the Sessions Court under
Section 302 of the Ranbir Penal Code, 1989, and sentenced to death.
However, the other co-accused were acquitted by the Sessions Court.
4. State has filed appeal against the acquittal of those accused
persons whereas petitioner has filed Criminal Appeal No.6/2015
before the High Court. In addition, there is also the death
confirmation reference. The appeal against acquittal along with
petitioner’s  appeal  and  confirmation  reference  were  clubbed
together.
5. However, since the Criminal Appeal of the petitioner is tagged
with the aforesaid appeal against acquittal and the reference, the
same has not been heard because in the appeal against acquittal
notice could not be served. We have been informed that the next
date fixed in the appeals and reference is 18.09.2026.
6. We notice that appellant has already undergone more than 16
years of incarceration. The fate of a convict facing death penalty
cannot be kept in an uncertain state in this fashion for 16 long
years. We, therefore, request the High Court to segregate Criminal
Appeal No.6 of 2015 from the appeal against acquittal and hear the
same along with the death confirmation reference expeditiously
within a period of 2 months from the date of production of a copy
of this order.
7. Special Leave Petition is accordingly disposed of.
8. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.
 (IRAMNAZ)                                       (CHETNA BALOONI)
COURT MASTER (SH)                               COURT MASTER (NSH)

Learned senior counsel for the petitioner pointed to the 
main relief sought for by the writ petitioner before the High 
Court and the impugned order dated 12.08.2026 pursuant to the 
earlier orders dated 02.07.2026 and 16.07.2026.
It was submitted that a writ petition was filed by one G.
Venkateshan  as  a  public  interest  litigation seeking CBI 
contd..

## Page 1317

- 2 -
Inquiry against the petitioner herein and the same being  
granted by the High Court, this Court by interim order dated 
24.03.3026 stayed the order of the High Court. That within a 
period of five weeks, another writ petition has been filed by 
the respondent herein virtually seeking the very same  
prayers; that the High Court could not have considered the 
submission made on behalf  of  the  Registrar  of  the  
respondent/University with regard to a Committee being set up 
by the Syndicate to inquire into the allegations made against 
the petitioner herein by way of interim orders as that was the
main relief sought for by the petitioner (respondent herein).
Hence, issue notice to the respondents.
Learned counsel for the petitioner is permitted to 
serve the standing counsel for respondent no.2/State.
There shall be stay of further proceedings of the 
Committee  constituted  by  the  Syndicate  of  the  
respondent/University, until further orders. 
The pendency of this special leave petition would not
come in the way of the writ petition being considered on 
merits by the High Court.

4. At the same time, we notice that an application under Section 17 of the
Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of
Security Interest Act, 20021 at the instance of the petitioner is pending before
the Debts Recovery Tribunal-I, New Delhi2.
5. Since measures have been taken by the secured creditor under Section
13 of the SARFAESI Act, it is appropriate that the proceedings before it be taken
to its logical conclusion by the DRT as expeditiously as possible, in accordance
with law.
6. We request the DRT to expedite its decision on the application under
Section 17 of the SARFAESI Act.
7. Insofar as the question of interim relief is concerned, we observe that the
interim protection granted by this Court shall continue for a period of a fortnight
from date with liberty to the petitioner to seek extension thereof by filing an
appropriate application before the DRT.
8. If such application is filed, the DRT shall decide the question of
continuance of the interim protection till the disposal of such application under
Section 17, on its own merits, without being influenced by any order passed in
this proceeding. All points on merits are left open for being urged by the parties
before the DRT.
9. The special leave petition is disposed of on the above terms.
10. Pending interlocutory application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.

IA No. 230910/2026 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING C/C OF THE IMPUGNED 
JUDGMENT
IA No. 230911/2026 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING O.T.)
 
Date : 31-08-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM :  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE UJJAL BHUYAN
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ATUL S. CHANDURKAR
For Petitioner(s): Ms. Meenakshi Arora, Sr. Adv.
                   Mr. Shyam Kumar, Adv.
                   Ms. Akansha Sinha, Adv.
                   Ms. Iqra Khan, Adv.
                   Ms. Kumari Ruchi, Adv.
                   Mr. Nikhil Jain, AOR 
  
For Respondent(s): 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. We have heard Ms. Meenakshi Arora, learned Senior  
counsel for the petitioner.
2. Delay condoned.
3. She submits that the appropriate Government did  
not form any opinion on the jurisdictional issue as to  
whether the respondent is a workman. According to the  
petitioner,  the  respondent  had  served  with  the  
1

## Page 1495

petitioner in a managerial capacity having supervisory  
character. Therefore, the reference should be quashed.  
In support of her submission, she has placed reliance  
on a decision of this Court in Secretary, Indian Tea  
Association versus Ajit Kumar Barat and Others, [(2000) 
3 Supreme Court Cases 93].
4. However,  we  are  unable  to  agree  with  the  
submission of learned Senior counsel, particularly in  
view of what has been observed by the High Court in  
paragraph No.61 of the impugned judgment. That apart,  
adequacy  of  the  satisfaction  recorded  by  the  
appropriate Government is not justifiable. Otherwise,  
we will be having two rounds of litigation, one prior  
to initiation of the Labour Court proceedings and the  
other thereafter, which is certainly detrimental to the 
interest of industrial peace and harmony.
5. That being the position, we are not inclined to  
entertain the Special Leave Petition.
6. Accordingly,  the  Special  Leave  Petition  is  
dismissed.  It  is,  however,  made  clear  that  all  
contention(s) are kept open.
7. Pending  application(s),  if  any,  shall  stand  
disposed of.

O R D E R

Awasthi, learned counsel, who has entered appearance on
behalf of the Respondent.
2. In light of the concurrent findings of fact based upon
correct appreciation of the evidence on record, we are not
1

## Page 1529

inclined to interfere with the conviction and consequential
sentence awarded to the petitioner.  The Special Leave
Petition is, accordingly, dismissed.
3. However, it is a matter of record that the petitioner
has been in custody for the last more than 15 years. His
prayer  for  premature  release/grant  of  remission,  thus,
deserves  sympathetic  consideration  as  per  the  policy.
Learned State counsel assures that an appropriate decision
shall  be  taken  regarding  the  premature  release  of  the
petitioner as early as possible and preferably within three
months.
4. Taking into consideration the period already spent in
custody,  we  direct  that  the  petitioner  be  released  on
interim parole for a period of three months or until a
decision on his application for premature release is taken
by  the  competent  authority,  whichever  is  later.  The
petitioner shall be released on interim parole on such terms
and conditions as may be imposed by the jail authorities.
Ordered accordingly.
5. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand closed.
